clue.text: Notice second trophy

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
a pot is slang for a cup or trophy won in sport

explanation.surface: Someone spots a trophy for coming second, a runner-up's prize.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of or observe it, a close synonym of notice as a verb.

clue.text: Bark and fight over last piece of bone

indicators.note: the final piece of a word is its closing letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a scrap is a brief fight or scuffle
the closing letter of bone

explanation.surface: Dogs bark and squabble over the final morsel of a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' in a down clue puts the fight on top of the bone letter. 'Bark' looks like a dog's noise but is the verb meaning to graze skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To bark your shin is to graze the skin off it, the same injury as scraping it.

clue.text: Companion wearing fancy Dior bloomer

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so these letters are rearranged
one who wears something has it around them, so the companion sits inside

blocks.note: the first part of the rearranged fashion name
CH stands for Companion of Honour
the remainder of the rearranged fashion name

explanation.surface: A companion dressed in elaborate Dior clothes looks like she is in bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: DIOR is reshuffled to ORID and CH goes into the middle. 'Bloomer' suggests a gaffe or knickers, but here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flowering plant, so whimsically a bloomer: a thing that produces blooms.

clue.text: Harmony provided by one North American musical instrument

blocks.note: acting in concert means in harmony or agreement
the Roman numeral for one
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A musical sound produced on a single North American instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A concertina is a small hexagonal squeezebox instrument related to the accordion.

clue.text: Dutifulness demonstrated by old boy and girl at northern church

blocks.note: OB is the usual abbreviation for an old boy of a school
a girl's name, short for Edith
N abbreviates northern
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A former pupil and a girl show their sense of duty at a church in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'at' simply string the pieces together in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedience is compliance with orders or rules, which is the same quality as being dutiful.

clue.text: Scratch dish

blocks.note: first meaning: to rub down or groom a horse with a currycomb
second meaning: a spiced meal of Indian origin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratch dish' sounds like a meal made from scratch; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To curry a horse is to scrape its coat with a comb, and a curry is also a spicy stew.

clue.text: Composer, in error, hid card G&S sent out

indicators.note: letters sent out are dispersed and scattered, then gathered in new order

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: A composer mistakenly concealed a card from Gilbert and Sullivan's post.
explanation.walkthrough: G&S (Gilbert and Sullivan) contributes just G and S. Richard Rodgers wrote musicals such as Oklahoma! and The Sound of Music.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Rodgers was an American songwriter who composed the scores for many Broadway shows with Hart and Hammerstein.

clue.text: Sovereign's small beard

definitions.note: possessive noun standing for an adjective: belonging to an emperor

blocks.note: first meaning: relating to an emperor or empire
second meaning: a small pointed tuft of hair below the lower lip

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a monarch's little beard; the two parts are separate meanings. The tuft was named after Napoleon III.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial describes an emperor's rule, and an imperial is also a goatee style worn by Napoleon III.

clue.text: Tiresome nanny and I go out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child sighs that the nanny is a bore, and off they both go.
explanation.definitionFit: Something annoying irritates, just as something tiresome wears one's patience thin.

clue.text: At home, see crazy silly painters instead of the parents

indicators.note: something silly is foolish and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: being in means being at home
loco is slang for mad
all eight letters are used

explanation.surface: An instruction to visit some crazy, foolish painters who live nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' only joins the pieces, inviting the solver to look; IN, LOCO and the rearranged PAINTERS make the Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In loco parentis is Latin for 'in the place of a parent', used of teachers or guardians taking that responsibility.

clue.text: One who tells amusing tales managed to take in company? True, funnily

indicators.note: to take something in is to admit or enclose it, so the word for managed surrounds company
funnily suggests oddly or strangely, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: ran as in ran a business
the standard abbreviation
the four letters reshuffled

explanation.surface: A storyteller managed to fool his audience, and true enough it was funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company?' with its question mark looks like the storyteller's audience, but it is just the usual business abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of anecdotes, the French-derived word for an entertaining storyteller.

clue.text: First to criticise article about river bird

indicators.note: the first of the following word is its opening letter alone
about means around, so the article wraps the river

blocks.note: the opening letter of criticise
an is the indefinite article
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A critic's first job: write an article about birds on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The article needed here is the longer one, not the single letter; the Po is Italy's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table, a domestic fowl and so a bird.

clue.text: Prove harmful to girl climber

blocks.note: to poison something is to harm it
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Something turns out to be harmful to a girl who likes to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' looks like a mountaineer, but it is a plant that climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Poison ivy is a North American vine whose leaves cause a rash, and it climbs trees and walls.

clue.text: Order a river fish

blocks.note: taken as written
R abbreviates river
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A diner orders a river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To array things is to set them out in order, and an array is an ordered arrangement.

clue.text: Where water board worker might be wasted?

definitions.text: Where water board worker might be wasted?

blocks.clueFragment: Where water board worker might be wasted?
blocks.note: surface reading: a place a water company employee works, where his effort is thrown away
setter's reading: the phrase means squandered, and water literally goes into a drain

explanation.walkthrough: A water board runs supply and sewerage; its workers deal with drains, and a wasted effort is said to go into one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for money or effort wasted is that it has gone into the sewer, the literal place for waste water.

clue.text: Before beginning of autumn, called into Gtr Manchester town for a plant

indicators.note: going into something means being put inside it, so called sits within the town
the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: Hyde is a town in Greater Manchester
called on the phone
the opening letter of autumn

explanation.surface: A phone call into a Manchester town about a plant, just before autumn arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' orders the finished town-with-call piece ahead of the autumn letter rather than inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The hydrangea is a shrub with large round heads of white, pink or blue flowers.

clue.text: Exceed Open record around the South

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for open encloses the compass point

blocks.note: overt means open, not hidden
S abbreviates south
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An Open championship score has passed the record held around the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' with its capital suggests the golf tournament, but it simply means visible or not hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstep a limit is to go beyond it, which is to exceed it.

clue.text: Boy, Rod, injured, found lying under steep rock face

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a cliff is a steep face of rock
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy called Rod is found hurt at the foot of a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'lying under' places the rearranged ROD after CLIFF. Rod looks like a name but is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Clifford is a male first name, and in crosswords 'boy' often clues any boy's name.

clue.text: Hamlet's halfwit?

blocks.note: surface reading: the Prince of Denmark, who feigns madness, or a fool in Shakespeare's play
setter's reading: a hamlet is a small settlement, so this is the local simpleton of a small community

explanation.walkthrough: The capital H points to Shakespeare's prince, who pretends to be mad; the word only means a small rural settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the proverbial fool of a small rural community, and a hamlet is such a community.

clue.text: Rower in line

blocks.note: first meaning: the oarsman nearest the stern who sets the pace
second meaning: a mark made by a pen or brush

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rower in line' sounds like a crew in formation; 'in' just links two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In a racing boat the stroke sets the rhythm, and a stroke is also a single pen mark or slash.

clue.text: Greek exaggerated over oxygen in cave

blocks.note: GR abbreviates Greek
OTT stands for over the top
the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A Greek tells an overblown tale about oxygen levels down in a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places one piece above the next; OTT is short for over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cave, natural or artificial.

clue.text: Steal a gun …

blocks.note: first meaning: to ransack and plunder
second meaning: a long-barrelled firearm

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue, building a crime story; this clue is just two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a drawer is to search and steal from it, and a rifle is a shoulder firearm.

clue.text: … to kill thugs, real worried

indicators.note: worried in its old sense of shaken or mauled, so the letters are tossed about

blocks.note: every letter is used

explanation.surface: Following on from the gun, a plan to murder that has the thugs genuinely anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links and 'kill' is a verb, matching the verb sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaughter is to kill brutally or in large numbers, a stronger synonym of kill.

clue.text: Chesterfield, third one in Derbyshire until now?

indicators.note: the third one in a word is the letter standing in that position

blocks.note: a chesterfield is a buttoned leather sofa
the third letter of Derbyshire

explanation.surface: Chesterfield is the third town in Derbyshire to be reached so far on a tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Chesterfield is a real Derbyshire town, but here it is the sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: So far is an idiom meaning up to this point in time, just as until now does.

clue.text: Solicitor protecting right of interfering old woman

indicators.note: to protect is to shield by surrounding, so the solicitor encloses right

blocks.note: a tout solicits custom, as a ticket tout does
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: A lawyer defends the rights of a meddlesome elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but it is one who solicits trade. TOUT wraps around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Old trout is British slang for an irritating or meddling old woman, and the crossword drops the old.

clue.text: Understand well-known person's not in

blocks.note: a public figure is a well-known person
out is the opposite of in

explanation.surface: Grasping that a celebrity is not at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure something out is to work it out or come to understand it.

clue.text: Hiker is not up to much

blocks.note: first meaning: someone travelling on foot
second meaning: dull and uninspired

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a put-down of a walker; 'is' joins two independent meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestrian walks rather than drives, and pedestrian writing or play is plodding and mediocre.

clue.text: Member with old construction kit

blocks.note: a limb is a member of the body
O abbreviates old

explanation.surface: A club member brings along an old building set.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is the Danish brand of interlocking plastic toy bricks for building models.
